sections.h2: Fridley housing and who buys it
sections.html:
Fridley is a first-ring suburb at the southern tip of Anoka County, just north of Minneapolis, with 30,829 residents as of July 2025. Most of the city was built between 1950 and 1970, so a lot of the housing dates from the postwar decades. Buyers will ask how old the roof, windows, furnace and sewer line are, so write the dates down before the first showing.

Owners occupy 63.0 percent of units, and the median home value is $302,900, which leaves roughly 37 percent of households renting. Investors and landlords are a regular part of the buyer pool. The city has 11,928 households, median household income is $77,680, median gross rent is $1,326 and the average trip to work takes 22.6 minutes.

Rent of $1,326 set against owner costs of $1,793 a month with a mortgage explains why some owners hold an inherited or outgrown house as a rental before they decide to sell.

sections.h2: City code items to fix before listing
sections.html:
Fridley enforces exterior and yard standards that a buyer's inspector or the city may flag, so walk the property first.

  • Grass and weeds taller than an average of ten inches draw a ten-day notice. If the lawn is not cut, the city mows and bills the owner.
  • Driveways must be paved or hard-surfaced. Gravel is not allowed.
  • Garbage, recycling and compost containers belong behind the front setback. They may sit at the curb only from 5:00 PM the day before collection until 9:00 PM on collection day.
  • Vehicles parked outside need current tabs and must be street operable, and cars cannot park on grass.
  • Fences top out at four feet in the front yard and seven feet in side and rear yards.

If a violation goes unfixed, the city can hire a contractor and add the cost to the property's taxes, or issue a citation with court fees of at least $300. An owner can appeal in writing to the City Clerk within 14 business days. Clearing open notices before the buyer's walk-through avoids last-minute credits. Take photos of the yard, driveway and fence once they are in order, in case a question comes up later.

sections.h2: Does a Fridley rental need a city license when it sells?
sections.html:
Yes, a buyer who plans to keep the house as a rental should expect to apply. The city uses two license subtypes: single family covers one to three units, and multi-family covers four or more. Applications go through the CitizenServe portal.

The owner must list a physical address, not a PO box, and an owner who lives more than 50 miles away needs a local contact. The owner shown in the portal comes from Anoka County records, which update every one to two months, so a new owner can upload purchase documents with the application. Rental licensing answers questions at 763-572-3616.

Selling a rental? Bring the current license certificate and any inspection results to the table. A buyer who sees clean paperwork moves faster, and a cash buyer can often close with tenants still in place if the lease is in order.

sections.h2: Stopping and transferring the water account
sections.html:
Tell the Utility Billing Division before closing, either on the Moving In/Out form or by phone at 763-572-3529. Staff need a meter reading on closing day to prepare your final bill, and the account switches to the new owner as of that date.

  • Residential water has a fixed charge of $26.01 per quarter plus tiered volume rates.
  • Sewer is billed on winter-quarter water use, and recycling is $11.60 per quarter for homes.
  • Weekly garbage service comes from a private hauler the city approves, billed apart from the city bill.

Unpaid utility charges can become a lien and go to Anoka County to be collected with next year's property taxes. Notices go out on or before October 1 for balances billed through July 31, and a 10 percent late fee can apply to past-due accounts.

Most of Fridley is in Fridley Public Schools, Independent School District 14. Small parts of the city fall in other districts: a northern area is in Anoka-Hennepin District 11, an eastern area is in Columbia Heights District 13, and much of the north-northeast belongs to Spring Lake Park District 16. Check the district for your exact address when you write the listing.

Interstate 694 and Minnesota Highways 47 and 65 are the main roads, and the Northstar commuter rail line stops at the Fridley station.

sections.h2: Recording a deed and paying tax in Anoka County
sections.html:
Anoka County records Fridley deeds. Property tax goes to Anoka County Property Records and Taxation at 2100 3rd Avenue, Anoka, or online through PayAnokaCounty. State law splits the year's tax into two halves due before May 16 and October 16 (Minnesota Statutes 279.01).

Paying online adds a 2.6 percent fee for cards and $3.50 for e-checks. Checks and in-person payments at the Government Center carry no fee.

sections.h2: Do I have to disclose problems with my house?
sections.html: Yes. Before you sign a purchase agreement, Minnesota Statutes 513.55 requires a written disclosure of material facts you know that could significantly affect a buyer's use and enjoyment of the property. The disclosure must be made in good faith. For a postwar house, think about old plumbing, past basement water, and any additions done without a permit.

sections.h2: Ways to sell and what each involves
sections.html: A traditional listing works best for a house in good shape, though it adds showings, inspection requests and loan approval time. Selling it yourself keeps the commission but leaves the paperwork and negotiation with you. A cash buyer takes the house as is, which helps with code notices, a tenant-occupied rental or an inherited property. Before accepting any offer, ask what the buyer expects you to fix, who pays closing costs and when you must move out. Get the answers in writing, and compare the net amounts rather than the headline prices.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fridley house that has code violations?
faqs.a: Often, yes, but check the notice first. The city can add abatement costs to the property's taxes, and buyers often ask for credits. A cash buyer takes the property as is, while a retail buyer may ask you to fix flagged items first.

faqs.q: Who do I call to close my Fridley water account?
faqs.a: Call the Fridley Utility Billing Division at 763-572-3529 before closing. The city needs a meter reading on the closing date, and that date ends the seller's account and starts the buyer's.

faqs.q: How much is deed tax on a Fridley home sale?
faqs.a: State deed tax is 0.0033 of the net sale price once consideration exceeds $3,000. Anoka County collects it, along with a $5 conservation fee, when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Does the buyer of my Fridley rental need a rental license?
faqs.a: Yes, if they will rent it. The city licenses rentals of one to three units and of four or more units, and a new owner applies through CitizenServe. They can upload purchase papers while the county's owner record catches up.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose problems with my Fridley house?
faqs.a: Yes. Minnesota Statutes 513.55 requires a written disclosure of material facts you know before you sign a purchase agreement. It must be made in good faith.
